rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human constitution and provision parallel one another: water is the origin of human formation and the basis of its sustenance.
rows.anchor: أن الماء بزر كون الإنسان كما أن الماء أصل رزقه

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: When asked who he was, the Prophet declined to identify himself and answered that they were from water.
rows.anchor: قال عليه السلام لمن سأله ممن هو فلم يرد أن يعين له نفسه : ( نحن من ماء )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth and heaven contribute to human constitution, and their roles in producing provision follow from that; naming them also encompasses their full extent.
rows.anchor: أن للأرض والسماء مدخلا في أمشاج الإنسان رتب عليه مدخلها في كون رزقه

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Prophet said that whoever usurps even a span of land will have it encircle him from seven earths; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: قال عليه السلام : ( من اغتصب شبرا من أرض طوقه من سبع أرضين )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth is mentioned before heaven because people's attention turns to what is below them before what is above.
rows.anchor: وقدم الأرض لأن نظر النفوس إلى ما تحتها أسبق لها من نظرها إلى ما علا عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The manifest proof of lordship persuaded most people, while their hesitation concerned messengership, so the passage follows lordship with a warning about the message.
rows.anchor: ولوضوح آية الربوبية تقلدها الأكثر وإنما توقفوا في الرسالة ولذلك وصل ذكر الرسالة بالتهديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition follows from both the command to worship and the reminder that God alone performs the acts just listed.
rows.anchor: ولما أمر بعبادته وذكرهم سبحانه بما يعلمون أنه فاعله وحده حسن النهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using the name Allah in the rebuke suits the condemnation of treating another as divine.
rows.anchor: قال معبرا بالجلالة على ما هو الأليق بالتوبيخ على تأله الغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the prohibition can answer the hoped-for taqwa: lā is then negative and the verb is subjunctive.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون مسببا عن التقوى المرتجاة فتكون لا نافية والفعل منصوب

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī defines an ند as a rival that competes in an attribute of standing and permanence.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : جمع ند وهو المقاوم في صفة القيام والدوام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb jaʿala suggests a descent from one state to another, through which heedlessness settles over hearts.
rows.anchor: عبر بالجعل لأن بالجعل والمصير من حال إلى حال أدنى منها ترين الغفلة على القلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People who see only creatures as sources of blessings and afflictions attach their hopes and fears to powerful beings, become submissive to them, and thereby worship false powers.
rows.anchor: حتى لا تشهد في النعم والنقم إلا الخلق من ملك أو ذي إمرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke targets people who claim knowledge: associating despite the proofs shows they lack sound knowledge and are like beasts.
rows.anchor: فإنه يلوح إلى أن من أشرك به مع قيام هذه الأدلة لم يكن ممن يصح منه العلم

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī argues that all creatures, high and low, depend on heaven, earth, and water, so making any of them God's rival contradicts necessary knowledge.
rows.anchor: كما قال الحرالي : إعلام بظهور آيات ما يمنع جعل الند لما يشاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse rebukes those who abandon the one capable of everything to worship what can do nothing.
rows.anchor: وفي تعقيبها لما قبلها غاية التبكيت على من ترك هذا القادر على كل شيء وعبد ما لا يقدر على شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This decisive teaching is shared by all revealed laws and scriptures and is the foundation of reverence, humility, and submission.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية من المحكم الذي اتفقت عليه الشرائع واجتمعت عليه الكتب

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says the passage trains the servant to turn sincerely to God by disowning the self, surrendering, serving reverently, relying on God, and resting in Him.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام أبو الحسن الحرالي في العروة : وجه إنزال هذا الحرف تحقيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The servant's fulfillment of the station taught by this passage is associated with the address to the tranquil soul.
rows.anchor: ويتأكد تحلي العبد بمستحق أوصافه لقراءة هذا الحرف والعمل به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reading and practicing the decisive teaching requires avoiding ambiguous matters, whose pursuit reflects the limits of reason; believers affirm them without comparing divine address with human inference.
rows.anchor: لأن اتباع المتشابه زيغ لقصور العقل والفهم عن نيله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has made the recognition of Him possible only through acknowledging that He cannot be fully known.
rows.anchor: سبحانه من لم يجعل سبيلا إلى معرفته إلا بالعجز عن معرفته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The decisive teaching is joined to the opening revelation, “Read in your Lord's name,” and to the first command in the Qur'an's arrangement to worship the Lord.
rows.anchor: وجامع منزل المحكم ما افتتح به التنزيل في قوله تعالى :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship of the heart is knowledge of God; the call first directs people to worship, then to know Him.
rows.anchor: إلى ما ينتظم بذلك من ذكر عبادة القلب التي هي المعرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship of the soul consists in patient steadfastness and good recompense; a humbled heart would make the limbs humble as well.
rows.anchor: ومن ذكر عبادة النفس التي هي الإجمال في الصبر وحسن الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commands, prohibitions, lawful, and unlawful regulate outward conduct and worldly or future affairs; the deeper teaching is exclusive loyalty to God and servitude to Him.
rows.anchor: وما تقدم من حرفي الحلال والحرام لإصلاح الدنيا , وحرفي الأمر والنهي لإصلاح العقبى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike outward observances that a hypocrite can imitate, knowledge, humility, longing for God, acceptance of decree, and love belong to sincere servants.
rows.anchor: وليس يمكنه مع نفاقه التحلي بالمعرفة , ولا بالخشوع ولا بالخضوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description of the Merciful's servants and the assurance that Satan has no authority over God's servants exemplify those who embody the decisive teaching.
rows.anchor: الذين ليس للشيطان عليهم سلطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the decisive teaching accords with the servant's created nature and relation to God, it remains constant across religions and revealed laws.
rows.anchor: ولما كان حرف المحكم مستحق العبد في حق الرب في فطرته التي فطر عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The decisive verses are the Mother of the Book, containing the four other modes that vary, abrogate one another, and differ among legal communities.
rows.anchor: فكانت آياته لذلك هن أم الكتاب المشتمل على الأحرف الأربعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who act on the decisive teaching are guided people of the Sunna and community; following ambiguous verses produces sectarian division, innovations, and misguidance.
rows.anchor: وقرأته العملة به هم المهتدون أهل السنة والجماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The decisive teaching brings unity and guidance, while the ambiguous teaching brings division and error.
rows.anchor: فحرف المحكم للاجتماع والهدى , وحرف المتشابه للافتراق والضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ordinary believers receive the four earlier modes of worship, while those fully realized in servitude know themselves as property of the Master, without a claim against Him even in assigning bliss or misery.
rows.anchor: قراءة الأحرف الماضية الأربعة هو حظ العامة من الأمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: From the heart, this teaching means recognizing creation's dependence in existence, provision, and divine direction: creatures possess no independent power, and surrender all inward and outward affairs to God.
rows.anchor: لا يملك لنفسه ضرا ولا نفعا ولا موتا ولا حياة ولا نشورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The servant's truthful religion is Islam; rational reflection and a purified inner core lead to Abraham's upright faith.
rows.anchor: وما يتحقق للعبد من ذلك عن اعتبار العقل وخلوص اللب هي الملة الحنيفية ملة النبي الخليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul's proper state is servile humility, gentleness, and freedom from pride over other creatures; this produces good conduct with people and truthful worship of God.
rows.anchor: جماع ذلك وأصله الذل وانكسارا والذل عطفا والبراءة من الترفع والفخر على سائر الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The limbs complete Islam by submitting to God in speech, action, and giving, while keeping other people safe from tongue and hand.
rows.anchor: وإما من جهة العمل فتصرف الجوارح وإسلامها لله قولا وفعلا وبذلا , ومسالمة الخلق لسانا ويدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text states that a person is not counted among Muslims until people are safe from his tongue and hand; it gives no transmitter or grading.
rows.anchor: لا يكتب أحدكم في المسلمين حتى يسلم الناس من لسانه ويده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer's lowered gaze and the right hand placed over the left at the chest express a servant waiting respectfully for an unknown command from the master.
rows.anchor: كالذي بنيت عليه هيئة الصلاة من الإطراق في القيام ووضع اليمنى على اليسرى بحذاء الصدر

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet sat for food in the humble posture of a servant and said, “I am a servant; I eat as a servant eats.”
rows.anchor: كان صلى الله عليه وسلم يجلس لطعامه ليستوي حال تعبده في أمر دنياه وأخراه ويقول : ( إنما أنا عبد آكل كما يأكل العبد )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following the Prophet, as commanded in 3:31, joins realization of servitude in the heart, humility of the soul, and submission of the limbs.
rows.anchor: فبهذه الأمور من تحقق العبودية للقلب وذل النفس وانكسار الجوارح تحصل قراءة حرف المحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument connects tightly with the earlier statement that whoever earns evil and is surrounded by sin faces the consequence described there.
rows.anchor: من كسب سيئة وأحاطت به خطيئته

words: وقالت اليهود ليست النصارى على شيء
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is feminine in “the Jews said” because their assertion is weak and their collective state is being treated as feminine.
rows.anchor: أنث فعلهم لضعف قولهم وجمع أمرهم

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī explains the negation as unrestricted denial of something previously asserted or presumed.
rows.anchor: ليس مخففة من وزن فرح , ومعناها مطلق النفي لمتقدم إثبات أو مقدره - قاله الحرالي

words: وقالت اليهود ليست النصارى على شيء
وقالت النصارى ليست اليهود على شيء
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each group denies that the other's religion has anything valid, even though each scripture recognizes the other's original faith; the contradiction makes their claim especially blameworthy.
rows.anchor: مع أن في كتاب كل منهم حقية أصل دين الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their denial is especially astonishing because they recite scripture that affirms the original truth of the other community.
rows.anchor: فعجب منهم في هذه الدعوى العامة لما قبل التبديل والنسخ وما بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “likewise” introduces the ignorant pagans, including idolaters and deniers, who make the same claim despite lacking scripture.
rows.anchor: ثم شبه بهم في نحو هذا القول الجهلة الذين ليس لهم كتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated “likewise” confirms that the report is literal, not a figure for something else, despite how astonishing the ignorant groups' claim sounds.
rows.anchor: فأجيب بقوله : { كذلك } أي الأمر كما ذكرنا عنهم حقيقة لا كناية عن شيء غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idolaters and other ignorant groups also misled believers, scriptural scholars, and followers of every religion by condemning them.
rows.anchor: فعاندوا وضللوا المؤمنين أهل العلم بالكتاب الخاتم الذي لا كتاب مثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arab idolaters had expelled the Messenger from his homeland and barred him from the mosque of his forefather Abraham.
rows.anchor: ومنهم عبدة الأصنام الذين منهم العرب الذين أخرجوا الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم من بلده ومنعوه من مسجد أبيه إبراهيم

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī describes God's judgment as restricting a person to some of the actions available to him and withholding others.
rows.anchor: والحكم قصر المصرف على بعض ما يتصرف فيه وعن بعض ما تشوف إليه - قاله الحرالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After these groups disagree, God will judge their dispute on the Day of Resurrection, affirming the resurrection and resolving their conflict.
rows.anchor: يوم القيامة فيما كانوا فيه يختلفون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb يعْلم is read in the subjunctive by readers other than Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir; the author says this has sound grammatical analyses.
rows.anchor: بنصب ( يعلم ) في قراءة غير نافع وابن عامر على بعض التوجيهات

rows.speaker: الرضي
rows.claim: Al-Raḍī says إذا normally points to a specified future time when an event is expected with certainty, which is why a verb commonly follows it.
rows.anchor: قال الرضي وهو العلامة نجم الدين محمد بن حسن الإستراباذي في الظرف من شرحه

rows.speaker: الرضي
rows.claim: A conditional particle requests two clauses: the first is a posited condition and the second its consequence.
rows.anchor: فالمضمون الأول مفروض ملزوم , والثاني لازمه

rows.speaker: الرضي
rows.claim: In contrasts with إذَا, إن marks a hypothetical future condition without the speaker's certainty that it will occur; this remains true even in divine speech.
rows.anchor: و ( إن ) موضوعة لشرط مفروض وجوده في المستقبل مع عدم قطع المتكلم

rows.speaker: الرضي
rows.claim: Because certainty and a hypothetical condition seem incompatible, إذا does not inherently mean إن; usage nevertheless permits a conditional sense when expected events can fail to occur.
rows.anchor: لما كان ( إذا ) للأمر المقطوع بوجوده في اعتقاد المتكلم في المستقبل

rows.speaker: الرضي
rows.claim: Frequent conditional use lets إذا introduce two clauses patterned like condition and consequence even when the event is certain and they are not truly conditional.
rows.anchor: ولما كثر دخول معنى الشرط في ( إذا ) وخروجه عن أصله من الوقت المعين

rows.speaker: الرضي
rows.claim: أن may be elided after ف or و following a condition or its answer because these positions resemble conditional and consequential clauses; the example continues with 42:33.
rows.anchor: وقد تضمر ( أن ) بعد الفاء والواو الواقعتين بعد الشرط قبل الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If “people” means the Arabs, the verse promises the Prophet that those already turning to him will be strengthened and those turning away will join his party.
rows.anchor: فإن كان المراد بالناس العرب فهو بشارة له صلى الله عليه وسلم بأنه يقر عينه بجعلهم من حزبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If “people” is universal, the promise concerns most of creation following the Prophet, with its full realization when Jesus descends and all follow the Muhammadan path.
rows.anchor: وإن كان المراد أعم منهم فهو بشارة باتباع أكثر الخلائق له صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding passage may explain God's distinction between believers and others as an act of justice, since treating the righteous like the corrupt would pain the righteous.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون تعليلا للكلام من أوله فيكون المعنى أن صفتي رأفته ورحمته مقتضيتان للتمييز بين المؤمنين وغيرهم للعدل بين الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prior discussion leads rhetorically to a change of qibla: after general mercy toward people, God shows mercy specifically to His Messenger by turning him toward the Kaaba.
rows.anchor: ولما أشعر الكلام السابق أهل البلاغة بإحداث أمر في القبلة فتوقعوا الخبر عن ذلك

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī reads the phrasing as an announcement to someone awaiting news and says قد signals the rarity of both the Prophet's turning and God's seeing it.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : فيه نبأ إسماع لمن يرتقب أمرا أو خبرا يفيد مع المستقبل ندرة الوقوع

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says the Prophet inwardly wanted the Kaaba, a qibla for all people, but relied on God's knowing his wish rather than asking; for one who asks, prayer obtains a need, while reliance on God's knowledge is worship.
rows.anchor: لأن الدعاء للطالبين قضاء حاجة وللمكتفين بعلم الله عبادة

words: قَدْ نَرَىٰ تَقَلُّبَ وَجْهِكَ فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ
rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī contrasts the worshipper, whose inward heart is his orientation and who should not raise his gaze, with the supplicant, who faces heaven and raises his hands.
rows.anchor: كما اختص غيب القلوب بوجهه المصلي , فالمصلي يرجع إلى غيب قلبه , ولا يرفع طرفه إلى السماء

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The passage cites a Prophetic warning that people must stop raising their eyes to heaven during prayer or their sight will be snatched; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: ولينتهين أقوام عن رفع أبصارهم إلى السماء في الصلاة أو لتخطفن أبصارهم

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī takes the indefinite qibla to anticipate a universal orientation to God, progressing from the Syrian qibla through the Hijazi qibla to an all-encompassing orientation.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : نكرها لما كان من ورائها قبلة التوجه العام في تنقله

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī distinguishes what God wills from what is approved: an occurrence becomes pleasing only when approval follows, while a later removal shows it was willed but not approved.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله : { ترضاها } إنباء بإقراره للتوجه لهذه القبلة

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The Prophet's visible face turns toward the Kaaba, while his heart turns toward God: the unseen belongs to the unseen and the outward to the outward.
rows.anchor: وأما قلبك فإنما توجهه إلى الله , الغيب للغيب والظاهر للظاهر

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī adduces Arab poetry to show that شطر means aiming at the very object when it is visible, and determining its direction through judgment when unseen.
rows.anchor: كما استدل الشافعي رحمه الله في الرسالة على ذلك بجملة من أشعار العرب

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says calling it the Sacred Mosque rather than the Kaaba broadens the expression; God called it sacred against entry marked by arrogance or confusion.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : سماه الله حراما على من يدخله دخول متكبر أو متحير

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Māwardī says “the Sacred Mosque” normally means the sanctuary elsewhere in the Qur'an, but here it means the Kaaba.
rows.anchor: وعن الإمام الماوردي أن كل موضع ذكر الله فيه المسجد الحرام فالمراد به الحرم إلا هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression suits a prayer context because prostration is prayer's greatest aim; the commentary returns to the phrase at 2:217.
rows.anchor: وعبر عنه بذلك لأن السياق للصلاة التي أعظم مقصودها السجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's mercy may uproot a sinner from his sins and place him where divine approval wills; the author says uncaused mercy excels in kind, while mercy answering a cause excels in its own force.
rows.anchor: فإن رحمة من لا سبب منه تقتضي العطف عليه أبلغ في نوعها من حيث كونها ابتداء والأولى أبلغ في نفسها لما اقتضاها من السبب

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib reports in the Muwaṭṭaʾ that the Prophet prayed toward Jerusalem for sixteen months after arriving in Medina and the qibla changed two months before Badr.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن المسيب أنه قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command “wherever you are” signals a third glad tiding: the community will multiply and spread across the regions of earth granted to it.
rows.anchor: أشار إلى بشارة ثالثة بتكثير أمته ونشرهم في أقطار الأرض

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī glosses turning faces toward it as directing one's acceptance toward God.
rows.anchor: بتوجيه قبولكم إلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The People of the Book here are Jews and Christians, who know the qibla change is true and from their Lord, though they rejected the mercy they had awaited in the Messenger.
rows.anchor: أي من اليهود والنصارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They know this change is the truth from their Lord and the final truth about the qibla, with no further change to supersede it.
rows.anchor: أي ليس بعده في أمر القبلة حق آخر يرفعه أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ending threatens the opponents while consoling, confirming, and strengthening the Prophet and his followers.
rows.anchor: وجعل ذلك سبحانه في سياق مهدد له مرج له ولأتباعه تسلية لهم وتثبيتا وتقوية لعزائمهم

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says the yāʾ reading turns away from the opponents, while the tāʾ reading addresses them; this marks continued bad conduct in two degrees, with the worse degree met by God's turning to others.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : بالياء أي التحتانية إعراضا عنهم , وبالتاء إقبالا عليهم
